note: Derived reading aid. Never authoritative; never read as intent (Decision 0004). The Plan document governs.
author: Clara (technical writing) via Claudia Atlas <claudia.atlas@agents.arcadia.local>
title: From an idea to a managed build, without hand-carrying it
purpose: Let a new software idea become governed coding-agent work, and then a reviewed build, without the operator hand-carrying it from planning to building.
serves: The Project outcome: a stated outcome is clarified, routed and driven through coding agents.
done_when: An idea typed once becomes an approved plan, then a build Action, then a running agent Session whose result is checked independently, while consequential steps still wait for you.
reading_note: The first half is done: idea intake, plan approval and the Needs you board. The three open Actions (launch, finish and manage a coding-agent Session) appear to cover the same ground as the Go Plan's continuation work. Inference from the two Plans' text, not a recorded Decision: read them together before choosing which to continue.

actions.title: Turn an idea into a planning task
actions.why: So a project idea typed once becomes real planning work, instead of a note that waits for someone to act on it.
actions.done_when: One command records the idea word for word and creates a ready planning Action with one approval.

actions.title: Turn an approved plan into the first build task
actions.why: Closes the gap where an approved plan still needed a person to write the first build Action.
actions.done_when: Accepting a plan creates exactly one build Action with full provenance, and starts nothing by itself.

actions.title: Prove idea-to-staging once, end to end
actions.why: A demo that the whole loop works on a real example: a blog idea becomes a site on staging.
actions.done_when: The MartianRover Field Notes idea became a Project, was approved once, and was deployed to staging only.

actions.title: Make what needs you obvious
actions.why: Your attention is the scarcest resource, so the queue leads with one item and says why, instead of showing every record at equal weight.
actions.done_when: Needs you shows one leading item, explains its ranking, and keeps work Arcadia can handle off the board.

actions.title: Approve a plan without reading raw files
actions.why: So you can judge a prepared plan as a readable page and approve, defer or send it back in one place.
actions.done_when: Review shows the plan readably, every outcome is recorded as a Decision, and nothing starts by itself.

actions.title: Start a governed coding-agent session
actions.why: The build loop needs Arcadia itself to start the agent, with every safety check, instead of you opening a terminal.
actions.done_when: An explicit launch option starts one tmux-backed Session, only after every check passes and a receipt is written first.

actions.title: Turn a finished session into the next step
actions.why: When an agent stops, Arcadia must record what really happened and what comes next, without treating 'it exited' as 'it's done'.
actions.done_when: Each exit is recorded once, the next state comes from the repository's records, and one real session proves the path.

actions.title: Run the build through to a reviewed candidate
actions.why: The last step of the loop: Arcadia runs the build, has it checked independently, and turns a failure into one clear fix, while merge and deploy still wait for you.
actions.done_when: A build runs in its own branch, passes deterministic checks and independent QA, and merge, deploy and similar steps still need their own Decisions.
